description.p: Vernier turns an architectural or engineering PDF into a measuring tool. Open the drawing, set its real-world scale once, and then take off lengths with the cursor locking onto the drawing's own vector geometry, so every measurement lands on a real corner or endpoint rather than an eyeballed pixel.

Set the scale either by typing the plot ratio printed on the sheet, such as 1:50, or by clicking the two ends of any dimension you already know and typing its length. Readouts come out in millimetres, metres, feet or inches. Placed dimensions stay on the page with their lengths labelled, and can be removed with an undo.

Pages render crisply at any zoom, with a thumbnail sidebar for multi-page drawing sets. Vernier reads any PDF, but snapping needs vector line work: a scanned drawing renders and can be measured, only without snapping.

description.p: First public release. Placed dimensions can now be deleted from their label or by right-click, with undo. Failures such as an unreadable file are reported in the window, and a page without vector line work says so instead of silently not snapping. A keyboard shortcuts reference was added to the menu.
Initial version: render a PDF plan, set the scale from a ratio or a known dimension, and measure lengths snapped to the drawing's vertices.
